decisions.executionNote: Begin inward elevated approach to basket with left arm and gradually pitch both wrists downward; board depicts the white cup with tan band.
Approach moving basket's left rim from above, finishing downward wrist orientation; keep right arm clear on right.
Use smaller increments after continuity guard; align left downward gripper with near-left basket rim as conveyor advances.
Center left fingers on moving basket's near-left rim, close and make a short retention-test lift; right arm holds clear.
Left grasp missed visually; basket has entered right workspace. Right approaches its outer rim to capture it while left clears leftward for the cup.
Raise right-held basket another 11 cm and inspect retention; left approaches image-matched tan-banded white cup from above in left workspace.
Use smaller steps to descend around the white tan-band cup and close left fingers. Continue a small basket lift and bring the held rim inward on the right.
Test cup retention with a small left lift. Basket did not follow the right hand, so reopen and descend onto its moving outer rim for a new grasp.
Retract left gently while lifting to avoid its reach boundary after the guard. Right descends with open fingers over basket outer rim, then closes.
Neither object followed prior lift. Reopen left to approach cup farther forward and lower. Move right outward above the actual outer basket rim, avoiding the handle obstruction.
Lower left fingers onto cup body while tracking conveyor, then close. Align right grip farther outward and descend across basket side rim before closing.
Test right rim retention with a 9 cm lift while gently retracting inward; keep left closed around cup without lifting until basket is raised.
Basket escaped and is tipping; reopen right and approach above its new position without contact while it settles. Lift/retract closed left slightly to test cup retention.
Cup escaped: recenter left fingers farther right over its visible mouth before closing. Bring right over the tipped basket's right edge, keeping the arms separated.
Advance left grip farther over cup using wrist view, then close. Right approaches the tipped basket's exposed handle on its right side rather than squeezing the broad rim.
Reduce left reach demand by lowering with very small forward motion after IK guard. Right finishes approach to exposed handle loop and closes gently without a lift yet.
Wrist view puts cup ahead and right of left grip; shift over body at lower height and close. Test right handle/rim retention by slow upward motion.
Relieve left IK boundary by gradually tilting fingers forward toward cup instead of extending EE. Right reopens and aligns closer and lower on the exposed basket handle.
Test the newly aligned cup and handle grasps with small vertical lifts, keeping both grippers closed and watching actual object motion.
Both prior lifts missed. Advance left farther over cup center before closing, and descend right toward the basket's now-horizontal near handle, aligning from wrist views.
Avoid left IK limit by pitching farther forward while lowering rather than advancing EE; align cup centrally in wrist view. Right approaches the middle of exposed basket handle from above.
Clear left wrist for an unobstructed head view of cup; prior closure did not center it. Recenter right fingers slightly left over the thin handle/rim rather than interior.
Separate arms for visibility and test the thin right-hand grasp by a 6 cm lift and rightward shift; keep basket grip closed.
Cup is now visible near center; approach its body with left arm without crossing the right arm. Raise and shift right-held basket outward to clear the center and test retention.
Replan with smaller approach increments and more forward wrist tilt to stay continuous. Close left on cup body near shared center; keep right basket grip closed and elevated.
Cup has moved beyond left's comfortable reach. Withdraw left; rotate the retained basket toward center for a left-hand handoff, keeping right closed and joint changes gradual.
Zero steps executed on prior rejection. Retry with much smaller left withdrawal and gradual right basket rotation, preserving the retained grip.
Basket is not retained after rotation. Park left safely; right opens and approaches the now-right-workspace tan-band cup with its jaw orientation restored.
Approach cup lower and farther forward with right arm, progressively pitching toward a shallow side grasp to maintain elbow-up continuity. Left stays clear.
Reduce translation and wrist-rotation increments after the continuity guard; continue a lower forward right-hand approach to the cup.
Cup is ahead of right fingers in wrist view. Advance and lower to its sidewall while matching conveyor motion, then close around the cup body.
Cup is right and forward of the jaw center; reopen clear of glue stick, shift right/forward around cup sidewall, and close without pressing lower into conveyor.
Cup is centered between right fingers in wrist view. Keep closed briefly, then make a small purely vertical lift to verify retention before transfer.
Prior lift missed; revise lower grasp height from cup and conveyor geometry. Open, lower the right hand and pitch more downward while tracking cup rightward, then close around sidewall.
Head view shows cup now farther forward than the jaw center. Advance the open right grip 6 cm at current height, tracking cup rightward, then close around its body.
Current fingers surround glue stick, not cup. Open and shift right while pitching farther forward to reach cup sidewall, avoiding further EE reach-limit strain; then close.
Cup remains to the right of the glue stick. Reopen and shift right while raising grip height above the stick, targeting the cup's upper sidewall instead of closing through both objects.
Cup body is now visually centered between the right finger pads. Keep closed, then lift 3.5 cm with a small inward retraction to test actual retention while preserving joint continuity.
Prior closure appears above the cup rather than around its wall. Reopen, align rightward, and lower 6 cm with the same shallow orientation to capture the cup body.
Fully open and raise the right fingers before further lateral alignment; avoid pushing the cup away while the gripper is still opening.
With right fingers fully open, turn the shallow approach toward the cup on the right and lower around its wall, limiting EE reach rather than extending the arm farther.
Advance in small continuous steps toward cup body, right and forward of the glue stick, and close only after the final alignment.
After IK guard, lower EE and pivot to a nearly horizontal side approach instead of extending farther forward. This advances the open fingertips toward the cup while relieving arm reach.
Keep right fingers closed at the lower side grasp and make a small lift/retraction to check whether the cup follows, without extending the arm farther.
Only the glue stick followed the lift. Release it and yaw the open, low right gripper toward the cup on its outer side, using wrist reach rather than extending the arm.
Cup is isolated ahead of the open pads and glue stick is left of the grip. Close fully, then lift and retract slightly to test cup retention without adding arm extension.
Use much smaller increments after continuity rejection. Reopen and move the right pads slightly higher and forward onto the cup wall, then close; cup retention remains unconfirmed.
At the right reach boundary, try a lower wrist and slight upward fingertip pitch with millimetric translations rather than extending farther high; close only after alignment.
Right IK is at its reach boundary and cup is not retained. Withdraw gradually with open fingers and unchanged wrist orientation to restore a safe extension margin.
Prior withdrawal executed zero steps. Retry with submillimetric initial retraction and no rotation to leave the near-extension configuration continuously.
Cup has moved beyond the current safe reach and is not held. Retract right arm progressively, preserving elbow-up continuity and clearance, and inspect the conveyor for a reachable opportunity.
Continue safe right-arm withdrawal with smaller increments after the rejected suffix; keep fingers open and left arm stationary.
